acceptance_criteria: Input bytes remain unchanged after successful and failed runs.
A successful run emits a cleaned copy and audit that explains each change and rejection.
Malformed quoting, ragged records, encoding errors, and ambiguous recovery produce explicit reported outcomes, not silent repairs.
Counts reconcile when record boundaries are known; uncertain record boundaries are disclosed without fabricated row counts.
Offline execution succeeds without network access or runtime packages beyond the chosen minimal runtime.
project.capability_gap: The catalog has no CSV/CLI implementation specialty. The two bundled workflow skills address contract definition and review; implement routine CSV/CLI work directly. No weak upstream match or untested custom skill is added.
constraints: All operation is offline; no external services, credentials, or network.
Keep original input files unchanged; never reuse the input path or overwrite it through aliases.
Produce a separate audit report identifying transformations, rejected rows, and uncertainty.
Runtime dependencies must be minimal; Python standard library is a reversible initial assumption, not a mandated stack.
Role documents only; no configured or running subagents.
project.deliverable: A cleaned copy and audit report, with explicit malformed-row policy and minimal runtime dependencies.
exclusions: No product implementation in this setup.
No browser, notebooks, deployment, external integrations, or agent configuration.
project.goal: Build an offline CSV-cleaning CLI that preserves source files and makes every transformation or rejection auditable.
project.next_decision: Specify supported dialect/encoding, allowed transformations, malformed-record recovery boundaries, report format, exit statuses, and output-collision behavior before implementation.

philosophy.approach: Define a small reversible end-to-end contract, then implement directly with standard-library tools where sufficient.
philosophy.evidence: Verify byte-for-byte input preservation, reconcile accepted/rejected records in the audit, and exercise malformed-input and output-collision cases.
philosophy.priority: Preserve input bytes and explain data loss or uncertainty before offering convenient cleaning.
philosophy.tradeoffs: Reject or quarantine ambiguous records with reasons; never guess repairs or silently discard data. Prefer fewer dependencies over speculative features.

project.users: People cleaning local CSV files who need to understand what changed and retain their original data.

roles.done_when: A bounded brief records observable acceptance criteria, explicit rejection/recovery policy, minimal runtime rationale, exclusions, and unresolved assumptions; no product code has been written.
roles.mission: Use the project brief to define the smallest offline CLI contract. Specify input/output separation, allowed cleaning, dialect/encoding, audit fields and reconciliation, malformed-record policy including uncertain boundaries, exit statuses, and collision handling. Preserve AGENTS.md and sample.csv. Do not implement the CLI or select external services.
roles.name: contract-author

roles.done_when: A review maps every material criterion to actual recorded evidence or an explicit unverified limitation and reports concrete defects; setup alone is never described as evidence that the CLI works.
roles.mission: Independently assess a future implementation against the contract with proportionate evidence: input hashes before/after success and failure, audit reconciliation, malformed quoting/ragged-record/encoding behavior, output aliases and collisions, and offline dependency behavior. Record uncertainty honestly. Review only; role definition does not start work.
roles.name: acceptance-reviewer
